newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish budget GDP forecast too optimistic - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Danish budget GDP forecast too optimistic - analysts.

text.p: Analysts and employers on Tuesday said that Denmark's draft 1997 budget was based on an over-optimistic forecast of 3.0 percent Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth and did not do enough to cut unemployment.

"I think that this 3.0 percent is way too optimistic and something like in a 2.0 - 2.5 percent range is more realistic for 1997," Lehman Brothers economist Keld Holm told Reuters Financial Television.
Hanna Duer, of MMS International, who also predicted 1997 GDP growth of 2.0 - 2.5 percent, said the government was perhaps premature in expecting a general European upturn in 1996.
"The government is anticipating a turnaround in Germany already this year and I don't imagine that will take place."
Employers' Federation Chairman Niels Fog said that the budget failed to take real action against unemployment.

"It is deeply disappointing that the government has come up with a budget proposal that is devoid of vital structural change to the labour market," he told Reuters. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
